blocks.text: Managing your workflow as a curriculum designer

Curriculum design involves balancing creative development with heavy administrative tasks. You spend nearly 40 percent of your time in the development phase. This is where PowerPoint becomes your primary workspace. If you find yourself clicking through the same menus, stop. Use your keyboard. On a Mac, most shortcuts follow a simple pattern. Replace the Windows Ctrl key with the Command key. For example, press ⌘ + Shift + N to add a new slide instantly.

When you work on multiple projects, keeping your files organized is essential. Use consistent naming conventions for your assets. If you are building a series of modules, consider keeping your master graphics in a separate folder. Link them into your slides rather than embedding massive files. This keeps your presentation snappy and prevents the app from hanging.
Using the Slide Master for consistency

One of the biggest mistakes is formatting slides individually. If you want to change a logo or a font across 50 slides, do not do it by hand. Go to View > Slide Master. Any change you make here applies to the entire deck. This is critical when you are updating curriculum materials for a new brand or a specific client request.

Lazur helps you navigate PowerPoint without breaking your focus. Hold the ⌥ ⌘ keys to ask about a setting. Lazur can point to the exact menu you need. If you need to write long descriptions for a module, hold the fn key to dictate. It is much faster than typing and allows you to keep your eyes on the screen.

items: Performance lag: If the app freezes, check for conflicting add-ins or background processes.
Syncing issues: Modern PowerPoint relies on OneDrive. If you are offline, your changes might not save correctly.
Subscription errors: Ensure you are logged into the correct Microsoft account to unlock all features.
Missing shortcuts: Mac lacks the Alt key ribbon navigation. Rely on your custom shortcut sets instead.

blocks.text: Keep your slides clean. Learners get distracted by too much text. Use the 6 by 6 rule. No more than six bullet points per slide, and no more than six words per bullet. If you need to explain a complex concept, use visual aids like SmartArt. You can insert these via Insert > SmartArt. This creates a professional look without requiring graphic design skills.

Accessibility is not optional. Always add alt text to your images. This ensures your curriculum is usable for everyone. You can find this option by right-clicking an image and selecting View Alt Text. Lazur can remind you where this button is if you forget.

PowerPoint is great for slide decks, but it has limits. If you are building interactive e-learning, consider tools like Articulate Rise. Many designers use a mix of tools. They build the core content in PowerPoint and then export it to a more specialized authoring suite. This hybrid approach often yields the best results for complex training modules.

If you are struggling with a specific feature, do not waste time searching menus. Ask Lazur to guide you. It will walk you through the steps one click at a time. This is especially helpful when you are using a new feature or working in a version of PowerPoint that feels slightly different from what you are used to.

faq.question: Can I use Articulate Storyline on a Mac for curriculum design?
faq.answer: Articulate Storyline is Windows-native. Most Mac designers use virtualization software like Parallels to run it, or they use web-based tools like Articulate Rise.

faq.question: How do I make my PowerPoint files smaller?
faq.answer: Compress your images before importing them. You can also use the built-in compression features in PowerPoint under the Picture Format tab.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside PowerPoint?
faq.answer: Lazur is a system-wide assistant. It does not click inside PowerPoint for you, but it can point at buttons, guide you through menus, and dictate text into your slides.

faq.question: What is the best way to keep slide layouts consistent?
faq.answer: Always use the Slide Master. It lets you set fonts, colors, and logos once, and it updates every slide in your presentation automatically.
